svg.title: Tariffs at the grocery store
svg.desc: Two perspectives with ten picks each. Differ Rank orders all twenty arguments by weighted impact. Exact ties use the earlier pick, then the permanent argument ID.
svg.text: Should the U.S. remove tariffs on imported groceries?

g.title: Checkout prices — Savings depend on retail price cuts.
g.text: Savings depend on retail price cuts.

g.title: Domestic growers — Give farms room to compete on price.
g.text: Give farms room to compete on price.

g.title: Staple foods — Food takes more of a tight budget.
g.text: Food takes more of a tight budget.

g.title: Food supply — Keep key foods in domestic production.
g.text: Keep key foods in domestic production.

g.title: Independent stores — Lower costs for small grocers.
Foreign subsidies — Offset selected subsidized imports.
Off-season foods — Imports can fill winter shelves.
Harvest season — Help farms sell as crops ripen.
g.text: Help farms sell as crops ripen.

g.title: Scarce local crops — Cut duties where few US farms benefit.
g.text: Cut duties where few US farms benefit.

g.title: Time to adjust — Phase in changes to planting plans.
g.text: Phase in changes to planting plans.

g.title: Food ingredients — Ease costs for US food makers.
g.text: Ease costs for US food makers.

g.title: Retail margins — Grocers may keep part of the cut.
g.text: Grocers may keep part of the cut.

g.title: Export barriers — Partners may lift duties in return.
g.text: Partners may lift duties in return.

g.title: Food processing jobs — Farms also employ packers and crews.
g.text: Farms also employ packers and crews.

g.title: More suppliers — More overseas sellers may qualify.
Trade negotiations — Exchange duties for export access.
Import paperwork — Track fewer duties on shipments.
Review each crop — Weigh each crop’s domestic supply.
Harvest shortages — Restock after a crop failure.
Targeted food aid — Reach households struggling most.

svg.text: Differ Rank weighs magnitude (50%), reach (30%) and duration (20%).
